title: A Mysterious Illness
text: Imagine a small village where the river is the only source of water. One summer, suddenly half the village fell sick with stomach pain, vomiting, and diarrhea. But the water looked exactly the same! What happened?

title: Socratic Thinking: The Invisible Danger
text: Why did water, which is essential for life, make them sick? Can water look completely clean to our eyes but still be dangerous?

content.title: Microscopic View of Water
content.description: Clean looking water vs water with germs.

title: The Reveal: Waterborne Diseases
text: Water can look clean but still contain harmful bacteria and viruses. Drinking this contaminated water causes 'Waterborne Diseases' like Cholera and Typhoid. Boiling water kills these invisible germs!

content.description: A disease caused by drinking contaminated water containing harmful microorganisms.

content.question: Which of the following is the best way to make tap water safe for drinking?

content.title: Reflection
content.text: Have you ever seen your parents or grandparents boil water during the rainy season? Why do they specifically do it during the monsoons?

title: Connection: The Monsoon Mix-up
text: During heavy rains, dirty water from drains can sometimes mix with our clean drinking water pipes underground. That's why waterborne diseases spread fastest in the monsoon season.

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Natural Filter
content.text: Take a plastic bottle, cut the bottom off. Layer cotton, fine sand, coarse sand, and small stones. Pour muddy water from the top. What comes out from the bottom? (Note: This water is visibly clean but still needs boiling to drink!)

title: The Tale of Two Places
text: Rohan went to a huge water park, splashing in thousands of liters of water all day. Just a few kilometers away, in a dry village, a young girl named Suguna walks 5 kilometers every day just to fill one small pot of drinking water.

title: Socratic Thinking: Fair Play?
text: Is it fair that some people have so much water they can waste it for fun, while others don't even have enough to survive? What happens when a place has 'Too Little Water'?

content.title: Water Scarcity Comparison
content.description: Comparing the massive water waste in urban entertainment versus the daily struggle for drops in dry regions.

title: The Reveal: Water Scarcity
text: When an area does not have enough water to meet the basic needs of its people, it is called Water Scarcity. Every drop wasted in one place is a drop stolen from somewhere else!

content.description: The lack of sufficient available water resources to meet the demands of water usage within a region.

content.question: If you see a tap leaking in your school, what is the best thing to do?
options: Ignore it, it's not my house
Put a bucket under it and tell a teacher or peon to fix it

content.title: Reflection
content.text: Think about your daily routine. Do you leave the tap running while brushing your teeth? How much water goes down the drain completely unused?

title: Connection: Food and Water
text: Water scarcity doesn't just mean no water to drink. Without water, farmers cannot grow crops. No water eventually means no food on our plates!

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Water Detective
content.text: For the next 24 hours, become the Water Detective of your house. Your mission: Find any dripping taps, leaking pipes, or family members wasting water and report them to the 'Water Police' (your parents)!

title: When the Body Loses Water
text: What happens when you do drink dirty water? Your body tries to throw the germs out! This results in severe vomiting and loose motions (diarrhea). But in doing so, your body loses a dangerous amount of water.

title: Socratic Thinking: The Quick Fix
text: When a balloon loses air, it shrinks. When your body loses too much water, it gets dangerously weak (Dehydration). If drinking plain water isn't enough, what special magic potion does the body need to recover quickly?

content.title: Cellular Hydration
content.description: How a mix of salt and sugar acts like a key, unlocking cells so they can absorb water rapidly.

title: The Reveal: O.R.S.
text: The magic potion is ORS (Oral Rehydration Solution). Our body needs a specific balance of salts and sugars to pull water back into our blood. ORS saves millions of lives every year!

content.description: A dangerous condition caused by the excessive loss of water from the body.
Oral Rehydration Solution - a mixture of water, salt, and sugar used to treat dehydration.

content.question: What are the three main ingredients you need to make homemade ORS?

content.title: Reflection
content.text: Have you ever tasted ORS when you were sick? It tastes a bit like tears, doesn't it? That's because it mimics the natural saltiness of your body's fluids!

title: Connection: Sports Drinks
text: Have you seen athletes drinking colorful sports drinks during a match? When they sweat, they lose water and salts. Those drinks are just fancy versions of ORS to rehydrate them quickly!

content.title: Mastery Challenge: Lifesaver Kitchen
content.text: Learn to make ORS! Boil one glass of water and let it cool. Add one pinch of salt and one teaspoon of sugar. Stir well. Taste it! Remember this recipe; you might save a life one day.

content.title: Hygiene First
content.text: Remind students that before making ORS or handling drinking water, they must wash their hands thoroughly with soap.

content.title: Filtering vs Purifying
content.text: A common mistake is thinking that filtering water through a cloth makes it completely safe. Filtering only removes dirt; it does NOT kill germs. You must boil or chemically purify it.
